title: Extraction of Total Soluble Lipid from Ground Coral Samples
author: Rowan McLachlan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc4qiyvw

steps.title: Grind coral fragments
steps.instruction: Freeze coral fragments and grind them in a chilled mortar and pestle (or ice‑bath) to a homogeneous fine paste.

steps.title: Load samples into freeze dryer
steps.instruction: Place freeze‑drying vials (4 mL amber pyrex, Teflon‑lined caps) upright in the wide‑mouth flask, loosen caps but do not remove, snap the black rubber cover onto the flask, and insert the tube into the Quickseal valve.

substeps.instruction: Loosen caps of each freeze‑drying vial (do not remove completely).
Assemble vials upright inside the wide‑mouth flask (two layers possible).
Snap the black rubber cover onto the flask top.
Attach the cover tube into the Quickseal valve on the freeze‑dryer manifold.

steps.title: Turn on freeze dryer
steps.instruction: Start the VirTis Benchtop SLC freeze dryer; allow ~40 min for the chamber to reach –53 °C and 100 mTorr vacuum.

steps.title: Start vacuum and dry samples
steps.instruction: Open the QuickSeal valve half‑turn counter‑clockwise, wait up to 10 min for vacuum recovery, and dry the samples for 12 ± 1 h (maximum 60 vials per run unless a different vial size is used).

steps.title: Weigh and sub‑sample coral paste
steps.instruction: Weigh the total wet coral paste, then transfer ~1 g wet paste into a pre‑burned 4 mL freeze‑drying vial and store at –80 °C; archive remaining material in a 50 mL tube at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label and weigh empty Erlenmeyer flasks
steps.instruction: Label each 25 mL glass Erlenmeyer (E‑Flask) with a Sharpie, weigh each flask three times, record the average as the empty flask weight.

steps.title: Transfer powder to extraction vials
steps.instruction: Unscrew each freeze‑drying vial, scrape the freeze‑dried powder into an 18 mL pre‑burned clear pyrex extraction vial, cap, and return to –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Remove samples from dryer
steps.instruction: Turn the Quickseal valve to the off position, detach the wide‑mouth flask, switch off the dryer, remove the black cover, quickly tighten caps on all freeze‑drying vials to prevent moisture ingress.

steps.title: Assemble vacuum‑filtration system
steps.instruction: Set up the filtration assembly: 250 mL funnel, 47 mm glass frit, GF/F filter, metal clamp, rubber stopper, disposable test tube, and side‑arm Erlenmeyer flask (with foam ring support). Place a clean test tube inside the side‑arm flask before use.

steps.title: Set up retort stands with funnels
steps.instruction: Place retort‑stand rings (covered with tubing) to hold 60 mL separatory funnels, fit each funnel with a Teflon or glass stopcock, and position them in the fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare extraction solvent
steps.instruction: Using a glass cylinder and funnel, prepare the 2:1 (v/v) chloroform:methanol extraction solvent according to Table 1, add 50 mg BHT per litre, and also prepare separate containers of 100 % chloroform and 100 % methanol; wear PVA gloves.

substeps.instruction: Measure chloroform and methanol volumes for the required batch size (Table 1).
Mix chloroform and methanol to a 2:1 (v/v) ratio.
Weigh 50 mg BHT per litre of mixed solvent and add.
Prepare separate 100 % chloroform and 100 % methanol containers (≈100 mL each).

steps.title: Prepare 0.88 % KCl solution
steps.instruction: Weigh KCl, dissolve in Milli‑Q water to make a 0.88 % (w/v) solution in a 200 mL volumetric flask; prepare fresh daily.

steps.title: Extract lipids from samples
steps.instruction: Pour ~12 mL of 2:1 chloroform:methanol into a 250 mL beaker, use a 10 mL syringe to add exactly 10 mL to each extraction vial, vortex 30 s, record the time, store vials in a dark cupboard for 1 h; wait 10 min between samples (or 5 min if a second person assists).

substeps.instruction: Pour ~12 mL of 2:1 solvent into a beaker.
Draw 10 mL with a 10 mL glass syringe and add to the extraction vial.
Cap the vial and vortex for 30 seconds.
Record the start time on the datasheet.
Store the vial in a dark cupboard (no direct light) for 1 hour.
Delay adding solvent to the next sample by 10 minutes (or 5 minutes with assistance).

steps.title: Filter extracts through vacuum system
steps.instruction: One hour after solvent addition, pour each extraction vial into the vacuum filtration assembly, rinse the vial twice with 2 mL of 2:1 solvent, collect the filtrate in a disposable glass test tube, then turn off vacuum and disassemble the system.

substeps.instruction: Tip the extraction vial to collect particulate matter near the cap, then invert and pour the solvent into the vacuum funnel.
Rinse the extraction vial with 2 mL of 2:1 solvent, vortex, and pour into the funnel (repeat once).
Collect the filtrate in a pre‑labeled glass test tube.
Turn off the vacuum, unclamp the system, and transfer the funnel and any residue to a pre‑labeled aluminum weighing pan.
Remove the GF/F filter with forceps and place it in the same pan.

steps.title: Transfer filtrate to separatory funnel
steps.instruction: Remove the stopper of the separatory funnel, pour the test‑tube filtrate into it, rinse the test tube with 2 mL of 2:1 solvent and add the rinse to the funnel; keep the stopcocks closed throughout.

substeps.instruction: Open the separatory funnel stopper (stopcocks remain closed).
Pour the collected filtrate from the test tube into the funnel.
Rinse the test tube with 2 mL of 2:1 solvent, swirl, and add the rinse to the funnel.
Replace the stopper to prevent oxidation.

steps.title: Wash organic phase with KCl
steps.instruction: Using a clean 10 mL syringe, add exactly 4 mL of 0.88 % KCl along the funnel wall, replace the stopper, invert the funnel three times (releasing pressure each time), then let the phases separate.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 mL of 0.88 % KCl gently along the inner wall of the funnel.
Replace the stopper.
Invert the funnel three times, removing the stopper after each inversion to release pressure.
Allow the mixture to stand until a clear aqueous (white) layer sits above the organic (yellow) layer.

steps.title: Drain organic phase to E‑Flask
steps.instruction: Open the stopcock, slowly drain the lower yellow organic layer into the labeled E‑Flask, stop before the aqueous layer reaches the stopcock, and cover the flask with a small glass Petri dish.

substeps.instruction: Remove the stopper to avoid vacuum.
Turn the stopcock open and let the lower organic phase flow into the E‑Flask.
Close the stopcock before any aqueous phase enters.
Place a glass Petri dish over the E‑Flask as a lid.

steps.title: Rinse funnel residue with chloroform
steps.instruction: Dispense ~5 mL of 100 % chloroform into a 50 mL beaker, add 1 mL of this chloroform to the separatory funnel with a syringe, invert three times (removing stopper each time), and allow phases to separate.

substeps.instruction: Pour ~5 mL of 100 % chloroform into a 50 mL beaker.
Using a 10 mL syringe, add 1 mL of chloroform to the funnel.
Replace the stopper, invert three times (removing stopper each inversion).
Let the layers separate before proceeding.

steps.title: Add methanol to E‑Flasks
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 100 % methanol to each E‑Flask with a 1 mL Hamilton syringe, swirl; if the solvent remains opaque, add another 1 mL and swirl again.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL methanol to the E‑Flask.
Swirl the flask to mix.
If the solution is not clear, add a second 1 mL methanol and swirl again.

steps.title: Dry lipid extracts
steps.instruction: Place all E‑Flasks into the nitrogen drying rig, secure with zip‑ties, set the water bath heating plate to 55 °C, connect UHP N₂ at ~15 psi, and dry for 20–25 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Insert E‑Flasks into the drying rig and secure with zip‑ties.
Place the rig in a water bath on a heating plate set to 55 °C.
Attach the pipette‑tubing rig to a UHP grade 5.0 N₂ tank and set pressure to ~15 psi.
Dry the samples for 20–25 minutes.

steps.title: Weigh dried lipid extracts
steps.instruction: Turn off N₂, disconnect the rig, remove and dry the outside of each E‑Flask, wait 5 minutes, then weigh each flask three times; calculate lipid mass by subtracting average empty‑flask weight and control contributions.

substeps.instruction: Turn off the nitrogen flow and disconnect the rig.
Remove the flasks and wipe the exterior with a Kim wipe.
Allow flasks to cool for 5 minutes.
Weigh each E‑Flask three times and record the averages.
Calculate lipid mass using the provided formula.

steps.title: Drain remaining organic phase
steps.instruction: Open the stopcock again and drain any residual yellow organic phase into the same E‑Flask, avoiding the aqueous layer; discard the aqueous phase and replace the petri‑dish lid.

substeps.instruction: Remove the stopper.
Open the stopcock and let the remaining organic phase flow into the E‑Flask.
Close the stopcock before the aqueous phase enters.
Discard the aqueous phase in appropriate waste.
Cover the E‑Flask with a glass Petri dish.

steps.title: Dry and ash residue pans
steps.instruction: Place aluminum pans containing the GF/F filter and dried coral residue in a 60 °C oven overnight; weigh each pan three times, then burn the pans at 450 °C for 5 hours in a muffle furnace, cool, and weigh three times to obtain ash‑free dry weight (AFDW).

substeps.instruction: Put the pans in a 60 °C drying oven overnight.
Cool 5 minutes and weigh each pan three times (dry weight).
Transfer pans to a muffle furnace at 450 °C for 5 hours.
Cool 5 minutes and weigh each pan three times (burnt weight).
Calculate AFDW using the provided equations.

steps.title: Resuspend dried lipid for storage
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL glass Hamilton syringe, dissolve the dried lipid in 300 µL of 2:1 chloroform, transfer to a pre‑burned 4 mL amber pyrex storage vial, seal with Teflon tape, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label test tubes and pans
steps.instruction: Label all disposable test tubes with a Sharpie and engrave the base of each pre‑baked aluminum pan with the sample ID using an un‑leaded mechanical pencil.
